narrative:
On September 21, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 3,238 cases across 56 judges and heard 1,279 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 39.5%. This marks a slight dip from the clearance rates observed on September 18 (42.0%) and September 17 (41.5%), though it remains above the 35.8% rate recorded on September 15. The day's total scheduled volume of 3,238 cases represents an expansion in docket size compared to recent prior sessions, which ranged between 2,812 and 3,104 listings.

Judicial output varied considerably across benches. High-volume clearance was led by Justice C.M. Poonacha, who heard 141 matters across two causes lists totaling 197 cases, and Justice V. Srishananda, who disposed of 71 of 108 scheduled matters (65.7%). Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde also sustained strong disposal rates, hearing roughly 80% of cases across his lists. Conversely, outsized cause lists weighed heavily on clearance in some courts; notably, Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard just 1 out of 279 matters on an extensive single roster, while the Chief Justice's division bench (0 of 23) and Justice Pradeep Singh Yerur (0 of 54) recorded no hearings.

Stage conversions revealed that throughput remained concentrated in early-stage proceedings. Preliminary Hearings led major categories at a 52.9% hearing rate (199 of 376), while Orders and Admissions cleared 45.9% and 45.3% of their lists, respectively. Final Hearings converted at 27.7%, reflecting ongoing structural bottlenecks consistent with prior rates on September 18 (28.0%) and September 17 (23.6%). Writ Petitions constituted the largest share of the docket (1,458 matters) with a 34.9% hearing rate. In contrast, criminal matters showed greater momentum, with Criminal Petitions (52.2%) and Criminal Appeals (52.2%) both clearing more than half of their scheduled dockets.
